hints: Minimum velocity occurs where the derivative of velocity, the acceleration, is zero and changes from negative to positive.
Differentiate again to obtain $a=0.06t-0.6$, then solve $a=0$ for the minimum-velocity time.
Evaluate both $s$ and $v$ at that time; report the signed displacement but take $|v|$ for the speed.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Differentiate the displacement function $s(t) = 0.01t^3 - 0.3t^2 - 2.07t$ to find the velocity function $v(t)$:
$$v(t) = \frac{ds}{dt} = 0.03t^2 - 0.6t - 2.07$$

Step 2: Differentiate velocity with respect to time to obtain the acceleration function $a(t)$:
$$a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = 0.06t - 0.6$$

Step 3: Find the time when velocity is a minimum by setting $a(t) = 0$:
$$0.06t - 0.6 = 0 \implies 0.06t = 0.6 \implies t = 10\text{ s}$$

Step 4: Evaluate displacement and velocity at $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$s(10) = 0.01(10)^3 - 0.3(10)^2 - 2.07(10) = 10 - 30 - 20.7 = -40.7\text{ m}$$
$$v(10) = 0.03(10)^2 - 0.6(10) - 2.07 = 3 - 6 - 2.07 = -5.07\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Speed is the absolute magnitude of velocity: $|v(10)| = 5.07\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Thus, $s = -40.7\text{ m}$ and speed $= 5.07\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: A change of direction occurs when velocity is zero and passes through zero.
Set $0.03t^2-0.6t-2.07=0$ and select the non-negative time after the particle passes O.
Keep the sign of the acceleration; it is not asking for its magnitude.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine when the direction of motion changes by setting velocity $v(t) = 0$:
$$0.03t^2 - 0.6t - 2.07 = 0$$

Step 2: Clear decimals by multiplying through by 100, then simplify:
$$3t^2 - 60t - 207 = 0$$
Divide by 3:
$$t^2 - 20t - 69 = 0$$
Factorise the quadratic:
$$(t - 23)(t + 3) = 0$$
Since $t \ge 0$, the instant when direction changes is $t = 23\text{ s}$.

Step 3: Substitute $t = 23\text{ s}$ into the acceleration function $a(t) = 0.06t - 0.6$:
$$a(23) = 0.06(23) - 0.6 = 1.38 - 0.6 = 0.78\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The acceleration of $P$ at this instant is $0.78\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
